audit.whatIsWrong: The two level charts disagree with each other and with the packet in five of seven rows. Content win[] gave Sett levels 1, 2, 6 and first item while its own whys[] text says 'You out-sustain his level-1 trades', 'Even at 2' and 'Even at 6'.
audit.why: packet.levelChart is Gragas, Skill, Sett, Sett, Skill, Sett, Skill, and the prose already argues exactly that. Full phases[] was flatly Sett-favoured 3/10 through level 3, which is not a 50.22% matchup.
audit.corrected: Level 1 Gragas, Level 2 even, Level 3 Sett, Levels 4-5 Sett, Level 6 even, first item Sett, two items even.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1 was written as a Sett stage. Sett has no ranged tool at level 1 — Knuckle Down empowers autos, Haymaker needs stored Grit, so Barrel Roll's 850 range is uncontested.
audit.why: enemyKit Q range 0 ('next two attacks'), W is 'Sett passively stores damage he takes as Grit'. He cannot answer poke he has not been damaged into charging.
audit.corrected: Level 1 belongs to Gragas; Sett's first real spike is level 3 with Haymaker charged (18/16.5/15/13.5/12s), and first item.

audit.whatIsWrong: Facebreaker is described everywhere as a 'pull-stun'. It only STUNS when enemies are on opposite sides of Sett — one side and they are slowed instead. In a clean 1v1 with no minion behind you it is a slow, not a stun.
audit.why: Riot text: 'Sett pulls in all enemies on opposite sides of him ... If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned.' This changes whether his all-in actually locks you, which is the whole basis of the trading advice.
audit.corrected: Stay on one side of him and Facebreaker is only a slow; the stun is what he gets by pulling you across a minion or a second target. E cooldown 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s.

audit.why: ownerKit E cd is 14/13.5/13/12.5/12 — 14s at rank 1.
All four suspectNames ('Use Explosive Cask', 'Hit The Show Stopper', "Drunken Rage's", 'Show Stopper') are false positives — the names match the kits.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Haymaker's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Sett edges 4-5 — a charged Haymaker's true-damage core outpaces your pre-max W. Bait his 15s Facebreaker, then take the trade.

edits.before: Riftmaker is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Haymaker's cooldown.
edits.after: Riftmaker helps, but Grit scales off the HP you give him — first item still leans Sett.

edits.before: Body-slamming INTO his answer — a whiffed E is 13 seconds of being a barrel with no plan.
edits.after: Body-slamming into a loaded Haymaker — a whiffed E leaves you 14 seconds with no exit.

edits.before: Sett wastes Haymaker — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Facebreaker stuns only if enemies are on both sides.

edits.before: Track Sett's Haymaker: His shield + true-damage burst. Burst after it. When it is down — E-Q burst him.
edits.after: Haymaker is a shield plus a true-damage core, charged by the damage you deal him. Trade in bursts, never grind.

edits.before: Sett edges level 1 — his Pit Grit punches hit harder than your single ability before Happy Hour is online, so don't contest the first wave. At Level 2 take Q+W and the lane flips even: your drink-empowered auto plus the Happy Hour heal-tick lets you grind trades, and his Haymaker only charges off damage he takes, so a short poke-and-back denies him Grit. The danger is his E, Facebreaker — never sit in auto range while it's up, because the pull-stun chains into his passive punches and a released Haymaker. By Level 3 he's slightly ahead again since your W and Q aren't maxed and your cooldowns are long, so farm with Q tip and wait for 6.
edits.after: Level 1 is yours — Barrel Roll pokes from 850 range and Sett has nothing that reaches back until he has been damaged into charging Grit. At Level 2 it evens out: your drink-empowered auto plus the Happy Hour heal-tick lets you grind trades, and his Haymaker only charges off damage he takes, so a short poke-and-back denies him Grit. His E, Facebreaker, only stuns when enemies are on opposite sides of him — stay on one side and it is just a slow; the stun comes when he pulls you across a minion. By Level 3 he's ahead since your W and Q aren't maxed and his 15s Haymaker is loaded, so farm with Q tip and wait for 6.

edits.before: You out-sustain his level-1 trades once you grab Q — drink-empowered autos and Happy Hour heal through his Pit Grit punches before he can charge meaningful Grit.
edits.after: Level 1 is yours outright — Barrel Roll reaches 850 while Sett has no ranged tool at all, and Haymaker cannot charge until you have already given him damage to store.

notes: Biggest fix here is Facebreaker: every line on the page called it a pull-stun, but Riot's text makes the stun conditional on enemies being on opposite sides of Sett — one side is a slow. That single rule decides whether his all-in locks you. Second, the content win[] chart and its own whys[] text disagreed in five of seven rows; both charts now match packet.levelChart. Note packet.games is 462 while the brief header says 1299 — I used the packet figure for confidence, and the win rate 50.22% supports the even framing that is already on the page.
